_comment: Issue #1144: SoldierBodies.step() used to pick its engaged bodies with engaged_soldier_indices(), whose depth comes from weapon REACH (engaged_ranks). A spear regiment's reach depth (6 ranks) meets or exceeds a shallow block's actual depth, so every soldier landed in the tier and the unengaged bulk -- the reference step()'s engaged branch is written against -- disappeared, leaving the block's rank/file order to churn indefinitely (soldiers visibly sliding sideways mid-melee). This stages exactly that case and shows it holding instead: two 45-man Spearmen phalanxes, 9 files wide and so only 5 ranks deep against a 6-rank reach, grind head-on for the whole clip. Team 1 is left on its own auto-advance; team 0 is ordered straight into it at tick 12 so the lines meet square rather than at an angle. The engaged-soldier highlight (Settings.show_engaged_highlight) is on, and it shows the MELEE tier, not the new body-contact one -- that dev visual reads engaged_soldier_indices(), which this change deliberately leaves alone. So the amber tint covers both whole blocks, which is correct and is itself the point: every rank of a 5-rank block really is within a 6-rank spear's reach and really can strike. What changed is invisible to that overlay, because the body-dynamics tier is consumed only by the physics step. The visible evidence is the formation itself -- watch the ranks and files stay legible through the grind, where before every man drifted across his neighbours' places.
